First-year students, Gram-negative cells appear pink at the end of Gram staining because they lose the purple crystal violet-iodine complex. During the decolourising process, gram-negative cells have a thin peptidoglycan layer and an outer membrane, which allows the alcohol or acetone to penetrate and remove the purple complex. As a result, the cells appear pink or red under the microscope.

When the demand for rice is elastic, it means that a small price increase can lead to a big drop in the quantity demanded. In the example, a 10 percent increase in the price of rice led to a 25 percent drop in the quantity demanded. This shows that consumers are very sensitive to price changes and will quickly switch to alternative products if the price of rice goes up too much. As a result, the revenue from selling rice will decrease when the price increases.

Cassava must be processed before it is eaten to reduce the hazard of hydrogen cyanide, which is released when the plant tissue is damaged. This hazard is due to the presence of cyanogenic glucosides, mainly linamarin, in the roots. When the roots are grated, packed into sacks, and left to ferment, the enzyme linamarase can act on linamarin, and the hydrogen cyanide is driven off. Proper processing, such as grating, fermenting, and roasting, helps to minimize the risk of konzo, a paralytic disease, by lowering the cyanide content in the finished flour to a safe reference limit of 10 mg per kg.

[P04] (AGR 203: Cassava processing and cyanide)
Cassava roots contain cyanogenic glucosides, mainly linamarin, which release hydrogen cyanide when the plant tissue is damaged. Processing reduces this hazard. To make garri, peeled roots are grated, packed into sacks and left to ferment for two to four days while water is pressed out; the mash is then sieved and roasted. Grating breaks the cells so that the enzyme linamarase can act on linamarin, and roasting drives off much of the remaining hydrogen cyanide. Sun-drying of thin chips also lowers cyanide content, but more slowly. For this course, a total cyanide content of 10 mg per kg in the finished flour is the reference safety limit. Poorly processed cassava has been linked to konzo, a paralytic disease, in communities that depend heavily on cassava during food shortages.

[P07] (STA 111: Mean, median and mode)
Measures of central tendency summarise a data set with a single typical value. The arithmetic mean is the sum of the values divided by the number of values. The median is the middle value when the data are arranged in order; with an even number of values it is the average of the two middle values. The mode is the value that occurs most often, and a data set may have more than one mode or none. For the quiz scores 4, 7, 7, 9 and 13, the sum is 40, so the mean is 8; the median is 7; and the mode is 7. The mean is sensitive to extreme values, so when a data set contains outliers the median often gives a better picture of a typical value.
